title: Melchiorre Biglia, nuncio in Vienna, 1565: two cipher letters (Ambrosiana, Trotti 22), second letter read

documents.shelfmark: Milan, Veneranda Biblioteca Ambrosiana, Trotti 22, fols 6v-7v

plaintext.source: Letter-book copy, entirely in cipher; no contemporary decipherment.

system.summary: Numerical syllabic cipher: single digits = vowel or bare consonant, two digits = row consonant + column vowel, a few codes (59 qua, 97 che, 19 per) and a small nomenclator; words separated by 00

prior_solution.where: Not in the repository; H. Dengel, Nuntiaturberichte aus Deutschland II/5 (1926) uses this register but prints neither cipher letter; web search on read phrases negative (29 Oct 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Syllabic grid (row consonant x column vowel) recovered by annealing on the training part, then refined by hand (K5d).
Frozen key on the held-out part (letter 1, 7r lines 3-27): lexical agreement 0.761 vs at most 0.500 for 200 controls (threshold 0.65).
Word-by-word reading frozen before counting; letter 2 at 95.0%, letter 1 at 94.5%.

outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the ciphertext alone and validated on a held-out portion of letter 1 against 200 controls.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Letter 2: 362/381 cipher words read in their sense (313 certain, 42 probable, 7 restored, 19 unresolved). Letter 1 (94.5%) not included.

credits.note: transcription, key reconstructed from ciphertext and validated on a held-out part, letter 2 read and translated
credits.source: Brice Dudout, email of 29 Oct 2026 (branch dudout/bundle-spain-italy, merged 30 Oct 2026)

texts.label: Letter 2, Vienna, [5] December 1565 (fol. 7r l. 33 - 7v l. 23)
texts.summary: Biglia answers reproaches for a bad start to the negotiation that offended the Emperor; the offer of 4,000 foot or 2,000 horse; a person of the Emperor's blood as their head; Zasius and Weber of the privy council dine with him and speak of the connubio.

reading_review.note: reading.md and translation.md read as sentences: the opening (the reproofs received, the bad start of the negotiation, the Emperor offended), the offer of 4,000 foot or 2,000 horse with a person of the Emperor's blood at their head, and the visit of Doctors Zasius and Weber on the connubio all build; the holes (19 words of 381) fall inside two or three sentences, and many words are probable {x} readings, so the text is coherent but raw (grade B). The 95.0% sits exactly on the bar.

gaps.item: 19 unresolved words of letter 2 (7r l. 38-41 and 7v ll. 10-23), each in a sentence otherwise read
letter 1 (fols 6v-7r l. 27; 729 words, 94.5% read, 40 unresolved): the contributor has not published its text, so it is not shown here
